topic: Discrete Convolutions: From Image Blurring to Feature Detection
target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science or Data Science students

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The 'Moving Window' Concept
lecture_lines: Imagine a magnifying glass sliding over data.
This filter captures local pixel patterns.
It slides, computes, and shifts sequentially.
animations: Fade in a small rectangular window labeled 'Filter' in #ffffff at coordinate D3.
Slide the window across a static grid of pixel data displayed at D4.
Highlight the interaction between window values and pixel values using a flashing yellow color #ffcc00.

sections.title: Mathematical Mechanics (The Sliding Dot Product)
lecture_lines: Multiply filter values by underlying pixels.
Sum these values into one new pixel.
This defines a single discrete convolution.
animations: Display the MathTex dot product formula: r'\\sum x_i \\cdot w_i' in #ffffff.
Highlight the sliding window as a vector moving across pixel values in a grid.
Show each multiplication pair (x_i * w_i) and update the sum total dynamically.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Local Influence
lecture_lines: Each output pixel gathers local influence.
Spatial information flows into synthesized results.
animations: Fade in a local 3x3 pixel region marked in #ffcc00.
Draw a box highlighting how the 3x3 neighbors influence the center output pixel.
Animate a colored glow propagating from the neighbor pixels to the resulting output pixel.

sections.title: Application: The Edge Detector
lecture_lines: The Sobel operator highlights intensity changes.
animations: Show a Sobel filter kernel with color #00ff00 to detect edges.
Slide the Sobel kernel over an image, updating the output pixel intensity dynamically.
Display a side-by-side comparison of the original image (D3) and the edge-detected result (D4).

sections.title: Real-World Impact: Neural Networks
lecture_lines: CNNs learn these filter patterns automatically.
Edges form the foundation for features.
Filters stack to recognize complex objects.
animations: Visualize a sequence of convolution layers as stacked blocks.
Show pixels transitioning from raw grayscale to structural feature maps.
Show stacked layers culminating in a 'Result' label with classification confidence.
